who: Henry M. Cowles, historian of science and medicine at the University of Michigan; PhD Princeton, 2015.

evidence.says: The authority cites the Michigan faculty page for Henry M. Cowles, historian of modern science and medicine, with a Princeton PhD in 2015.
Princeton lists Henry M. Cowles as a 2015 history graduate, with the dissertation A Method Only: The Evolving Meaning of Science in the United States, 1830-1910.
The department welcomes Henry Cowles to Michigan and identifies his doctorate as Princeton, 2015, and his field as the history of modern science.

notes: The LC record itself supplies the matching institution, field, and doctorate; select Henry M. Cowles among the supplied namesakes.

who: William M. Daly, medieval historian at Boston College, 1947-1986; doctorate completed at Brown, 1955.

evidence.says: Boston College identifies William M. Daly as its history professor from 1947 to 1986 and records his 1955 Brown dissertation on the concept of Christendom in crusade chronicles.
William Merrigan Daly is identified as a pianist, composer, orchestrator, and conductor, rather than the Boston College medieval historian.
William T. Daly is identified as a professor of political science at Stockton State College.
William P. Daly is represented by National diocesan salary survey, c1990; the authority provides no university or doctorate information.

notes: The supervisor is securely identified, but none of the thirteen supplied authority records establishes a link to him. Several are demonstrably namesakes; sparse records prevent a definitive rejection of every candidate.

who: Karl H. Dannenfeldt, historian at Arizona State University; PhD University of Chicago.

evidence.says: ASU lists Karl H. Dannenfeldt, appointed in 1956, as professor emeritus of history and dean emeritus, with a PhD from the University of Chicago.
The university archive identifies Karl H. Dannenfeldt as professor and dean of history and academic vice president.
The Karl H. Dannenfeldt authority cites his The Renaissance: medieval or modern? (1959).

notes: The full name, historical field, ASU affiliation, and Chicago doctorate agree with the supervisor record.

who: Amira Rose Davis, historian of twentieth-century sport, formerly at Penn State and subsequently UT Austin; PhD Johns Hopkins, 2016.

evidence.says: Her institutional CV records a 2016 Johns Hopkins history PhD, Penn State appointments from 2016 through June 2022, and a UT Austin appointment beginning July 2022. It also lists supervision of a Penn State Deportistas! dissertation project.
The authority identifies Dr. Amira Rose Davis at UT Austin, specializing in twentieth-century history and sport, and cites Go, Wilma, Go! and the manuscript Can’t Eat a Medal.

notes: The CV and LC record share the UT Austin appointment and works; the CV supplies the matching doctorate and earlier Penn State career. Her move precedes the student’s 2023 completion.

who: Roy José DeCarvalho, historian of psychology at the University of North Texas; doctorate from Wisconsin-Madison.

evidence.says: The 1996 article James F. T. Bugental: Portrait of a Humanistic Psychologist lists Roy Jose deCarvalho with the History Department, University of North Texas.
The publisher identifies the author of The Founders of Humanistic Psychology as Roy Jose DeCarvalho, with a doctorate from Wisconsin-Madison and research in the history of psychology.
Wisconsin lists Roy Jose DeCarvalho’s The Founders of Humanistic Psychology among alumni books and states that it was revised from a UW dissertation.
The authority identifies Roy José DeCarvalho through The founders of humanistic psychology (1991).

notes: The distinctive full name and book connect the authority to the Wisconsin-trained historian publishing from North Texas near the student’s dissertation year.

who: Robert Harry Detrick, associate professor of history at North Texas State University; PhD Indiana University.

evidence.says: The 1982-1983 graduate catalog identifies Robert Harry Detrick as associate professor of history, with an AM and PhD from Indiana University.
The 1972-1973 catalog also identifies Robert Harry Detrick as a history faculty member with an Indiana doctorate.
The supplied R. Blaine Detrick authority is based on Golf and the Gospel (1985); it supplies no academic affiliation or doctorate.

notes: The university identifies the supervisor as Robert Harry, whereas the candidate uses R. Blaine. No evidence connects these names or the candidate’s work to the North Texas historian; do not merge.

who: Leslie Dianne Dossey, historian of late antiquity at Loyola University Chicago; PhD Harvard, 1998.

evidence.says: Loyola identifies Leslie Dossey as associate professor of history, with a Harvard PhD in 1998, and author of Peasant and Empire in Christian North Africa (2010). It records her service as undergraduate programs director in 2004-2009.
The authority identifies Leslie Dossey, expanded as Leslie Dianne Dossey, through Peasant and empire in Christian North Africa (2010).

notes: The same book bridges the LC identity and Loyola faculty profile; institution, field, and doctorate match.

who: David Lloyd Dowd, historian of the French Revolution at the University of Kentucky; doctoral work at Berkeley, 1946.

evidence.says: The authority identifies David Lloyd Dowd through Art as propaganda in the French Revolution (1946), citing a University of California catalog report.
The bibliographic record attributes Art as Propaganda in the French Revolution: A Study of Jacques-Louis David to David Lloyd Dowd and lists University of California, Berkeley, 1946.
The scholarly association’s review identifies Professor David L. Dowd with the University of Florida and subsequently the University of Kentucky, working on the French Revolution and Napoleonic era.

notes: The LC identity agrees with the Berkeley year and institution and the Kentucky historian’s field. The review places his Kentucky career before the student’s 1972 completion; it does not establish supervision through that completion year.
